newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon to hold first municipal polls in 33 years.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon to hold first municipal polls in 33 years.

text.p: The Lebanese government has decided to hold the first municipal elections for more than 30 years next June, a move described by the press as a bold step toward reforming the worn-out public administration.

"The Council of Ministers...has decided to set June 1 and 8, 1997, as the dates for municipial and mayoral elections," Information Minister Bassem al-Sabaa told reporters after a late night cabinet session on Wednesday.
They will be the first municipal elections in Lebanon since 1963. Elections were postponed in part due to the 1975-90 civil war.

The leftist as-Safir daily, which hailed the decision "as a bold step towards reforming the administration", said these elections were necessitated by the fact that many of Lebanon's 695 municipalities are inoperative or their members have died.
"The decision to hold municipal and mayoral elections is more important than the decision to hold the (recent) parliamentary elections" the daily said.
The terms of existing municipality heads have been automatically renewed and those who left office were replaced by government appointment.
Government critics have said that among the undeclared reasons for the postponements is the fear of some senior officials that their supporters would lose.
